By restricting the dominant support of each observable to a small capsule and controlling inter-capsule entanglement, Q-Capsule preserves useful gradient signals while retaining communication between local quantum representations. As the register width increases, Q-Capsule consistently maintains stable gradient variance, whereas globally entangling baselines exhibit exponential suppression with a log-gradient-variance slope near -ln 2 per qubit. Q-Capsule also produces more structured optimization landscapes, higher parameter efficiency, improved robustness to depolarizing noise, and lower measurement requirements. Its adaptive policy achieves 98.1% accuracy on binary classification and 97.7% on four-class classification, while using approximately 73% fewer two-qubit gates than the fixed-deep model on the multiclass task.
n438adfe02ae4: As superconducting quantum processors scale toward hundreds of qubits, manual calibration becomes increasingly costly and difficult to sustain. Implemented within an automated calibration framework, the rules support a six-qubit Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger state with a zero-noise-extrapolated fidelity of 89.64%, distance-dependent logical-error suppression in a single-cycle repetition-code benchmark, and a reduction of the mean single-qubit error from 0.023 to 0.011 on a 337-qubit processor, providing an experimentally grounded reference for the automated calibration and maintenance of current and future large-scale superconducting quantum systems.
n5f6917b38c1a: The three gauge couplings of the Standard Model (SM) can be parameterized as the fine structure constant $α$, the weak mixing angle $\sin^2θ_w$, and the strong coupling $α_s$. To understand why minimizing magic reproduces both $\sin^2θ_w$ and $α_s$, we conjecture that the parameters of fundamental interactions among color singlets reflect a principle of quantum computational efficiency, with the physical universe emerging from a quantum simulation subject to constrained resources.
n5c539d47a1ca: Hyperbolic geometry hosts a plethora of exotic quantum phenomena ranging from holographic duality to novel topological phases. Here, we overcome these limitations by implementing a quantum simulation of hyperbolic geometry within the parameter space of a superconducting quantum circuit. By probing the systems' response under geometric quantum driving, we elucidate how the intrinsic geometry of the parameter space dictates observable physical quantities. Furthermore, we extend the theoretical framework to realize ensemble simulation. This generalization enables us to harness the fast coherent control of superconducting qubits to capture essential geometric characteristics, establishing a versatile platform for exploring quantum dynamics on hyperbolic manifolds.
nb76bbf6b7bf9: Randomized benchmarking (RB) with structured circuits is experimentally scalable, but gives biased short-depth fidelity estimates because incomplete ensemble mixing introduces transient modes. Here we overcome this obstacle solely through classical post-processing. We introduce a one-parameter family of estimators that interpolate between the standard LinXEB-type post-processing and a new post-processing technique we call the trace filter function. Under practical assumptions, the trace filter function provably suppresses transient modes, exposing an interpretable fidelity decay at short depth, with theoretical guarantees comparable to standard RB, at the cost of an increased variance. We bound the variance, analyze the evaluation complexity of the new estimators, and develop practical post-processing algorithms. Experiments on a Rigetti superconducting processor validate the method for one-dimensional circuits of up to 12 qubits: where the standard estimator requires depth beyond a 40-layer experimental window, the trace filter function yields consistent estimates below 10 layers. Trace-filtered randomized benchmarking therefore extends reliable fidelity characterization to relevant structured circuit ensembles and short-depth regimes that are inaccessible to conventional estimators.
nc3c5e6bcde67: We propose a scheme for generating and controlling remote nonreciprocal magnon--magnon entanglement in a cavity magnonic system with coherent feedback.The two microwave cavities are driven by independent single-mode squeezed vacuum fields, with a rotating YIG sphere in the left cavity and a stationary one in the right cavity. Coherent feedback enhances the entanglement at an appropriate reflectivity, whereas stronger feedback can reduce it. The relative squeezing phase provides additional control, and an appropriate choice of unequal squeezing factors improves the entanglement at fixed total input photon occupation. With the squeezed inputs kept fixed, moderate feedback also increases the critical temperature for magnon entanglement.Our results provide a controllable approach to preparing remote nonreciprocal quantum correlations in cavity magnonic systems.
nc20a69ab1d6a: Quantum compilers play a critical role in transforming high-level quantum programs into optimized, hardware-compatible circuits. Our findings indicate validation is dominated by program-content and program-metric assertions, and test circuits are generally small and shallow. Motivated by these observations, we introduce a testing methodology for automated validation of quantum compiler passes based on retromorphic testing and principles from the Hadamard test. This methodology analyzes a compiler pass, test circuit, and expected pass behavior to verify semantic preservation and intended structural modifications. We implement our methods in a framework, RetroQ, and apply it to compiler passes in PennyLane and Qiskit. n04c3d6d94355: Quantum key distribution (QKD) offers an approach for secure communication over quantum channels, based on the principles of quantum mechanics. The simulation results show that the SKR in practical scenarios, with parameters characterized from commercial QKD systems, closely matches the SKR under ideal conditions. In the finite case, the maximum transmission distance can reach up to 250 km with total pulse number $N=10^{12}$ and the SKR closely approaches the asymptotic limit up to 250 km with $N=10^{14}$. Furthermore, the feasibility and robustness of method in measurement-device-independent (MDI) QKD have also been demonstrated. n78d43a1dffc3: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) combine high quality factors with strong electromagnetic-field localization and are therefore widely explored for enhancing light--matter interactions. We emphasize some of the pitfalls associated with the numerical simulations, especially the utilization of periodic boundary conditions for fluorescence. Strong BIC-related fields can enhance acceptor absorption while useful fluorescence enhancement remains moderate. Extensive simulations and the comparison of different figures of merit, indicate that, while a BIC can suppress radiative leakage, it can also redirect a large fraction of the energy into Ohmic losses. As a result, the useful fluorescence enhancement of donors remains moderate, whereas absorption by acceptors can be strongly enhanced in Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET) experiments. It is essential to separate near-field FRET from long-range energy transfer and reabsorption mechanisms, both of which are mediated by the delocalized BIC mode. Finally, results obtained for finite gratings are compared with infinite periodic simulations and conceptual inconsistencies explained. This work provides a consistent framework for interpreting fluorescence, absorption, and energy transfer in BIC-based periodic nanophotonic systems.
na7791b724fb8: We investigate spin-outcome correlations and memory-assisted entropic uncertainty in tree-level Bhabha scattering, where an incident electron $A$ scatters with a positron $B$ initially entangled with a spectator electron $C$. In the parameter regions studied, enhanced $A|BC$ entanglement is accompanied by lower $U_A$, most prominently near high-energy backscattering. An analytic treatment of this limit shows that $B$ factorizes from $AC$: $G_B$ vanishes, whereas $G_C$ increases with the initial $B$-$C$ entanglement. These results show that initial $B$-$C$ entanglement can lower the total memory-assisted uncertainty in high-energy backscattering by strengthening spin-outcome correlations with the spectator $C$, thereby identifying the distinct roles of the interacting particle and the spectator as quantum memories.
naa7c1b8b84bc: An outstanding challenge in superconducting quantum circuits is mitigating loss from two-level system (TLS) defects. In the dressed-state picture, we fit the coherent swap oscillations to extract the TLS energy-relaxation time. These Rabi chevrons reveal coherent TLSs with a median energy-relaxation time of 10 microseconds, at coupling strengths previously associated with incoherent TLSs. The swap coherence times exceed the qubit T2* limited by flux noise, indicating that the dressed gap protects them from low-frequency 1/f noise.
n10912ad513a6: Spectroscopy with undetected photons allows the spectral response of a sample at long wavelengths to be measured through interference of a shorter-wavelength signal field, without directly detecting the light that probes the sample. The same system is further employed to detect sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) gas via spectroscopy near 10.55 microns. These results substantially extend the accessible spectral range of spectroscopy with undetected photons while retaining silicon-based NIR detection.
n3d8a4c9527e4: Multi-photon interference is the resource most native to photonic quantum machine learning, yet experiments on photonic reservoirs have reported advantages, null results, and train-only effects. Interference redistributes feature variance across roughly twice as many effective dimensions as distinguishable-particle statistics, generating a large geometric separation between the corresponding kernels. The separation grows superlinearly with indistinguishability, is linear in Hong--Ou--Mandel visibility at small visibility for two to four photons, and retains approximately 80% of its magnitude at the source quality of current quantum processors. Under experimental sampling budgets the separation is learnable on adversarially constructed tasks (accuracy advantage +0.22 plus or minus 0.05) and an order of magnitude smaller on natural tasks, gated by kernel--task alignment. The results reconcile the existing experimental record and supply a pre-experimental protocol: kernel geometry establishes that an interference-specific learning resource exists, and task alignment determines whether a given task can access it; both are computable before committing significant hardware resources.
n851080e6b50e: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is associated with increased oxidative DNA damage, while haploinsufficiency of BMPR2 and other dosage-sensitive genes contributes directly to disease. These findings define a sequence-resolved route through which repairable oxidative DNA damage could transiently reproduce loss-of-function transcripts encoded by pathogenic PAH alleles without permanent genomic mutation. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n3dd5958c34c9: Antiretroviral therapy suppresses HIV-1 replication but cannot eliminate the latent viral reservoir persisting in memory CD4 T cells. T4IL15∆ provides a robust reactivation platform that could complement other reservoir-elimination strategies toward an HIV-1 cure. ### Competing Interest Statement YH, MSN, JY, HM, and DDH are listed as co-inventors on patent applications filed by Columbia University on the use of described biologics for HIV-1 latency reversal. n9252e7b1518a: Aging populations face a growing burden of neurodegenerative disease and behavioral decline. The microbiota is increasingly implicated in host physiology, highlighting an urgent need to understand how gut microbes modulate brain function and late life health. Together, these findings establish microbial enterobactin as a non-canonical neurotransmitter regulating neuronal mitochondrial function, behavior and aging, defining a gut bacteria-brain axis with broad implications for maintaining late-life health. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
n81d668ae8b0e: Cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA), characterized by cerebrovascular amyloid deposition, is strongly associated with Alzheimer’s disease, ischemic injury, and lobar hemorrhages. One Sentence Summary Vascular-associated fibroblasts are a major source of pathogenic APOE4 that drives vascular dysfunction in cerebral amyloid angiopathy. ### Competing Interest Statement D.M.H. is on the scientific advisory boards of C2N Diagnostics, Denali, Genentech, Cajal Therapeutics, Acta, and Switch, and consults for Pfizer, Roche, and Annexon. n9e698a0c6960: Pooled Perturb-seq screens are often interpreted through a linear steady-state model in which each targeted gene supplies an additive perturbation input. This discrepancy persisted across random K562 target panels, an overdetermined Jost dimension sweep, direction-only fits, ridge and truncated-SVD estimators, and five linear ground-truth ensembles. n9eb593075e49: We investigated how auditory and visual presentation of small numerical magnitudes and non- numerical magnitudes are passively processed at the neural level. In the auditory paradigm, the standard stimulus was a 2-part sound, while the deviant stimuli varied in frequency, intensity, gap length, and number of sounds (1-part and 3-part stimuli). In the visual paradigm, the standard stimulus was a dot array containing two medium-sized dots, while the deviant stimuli varied in numerosity (1 or 3 dots) and dot size (small or large). The results for the auditory paradigm showed significant MMN across all features, including comparisons with deviant-alone control stimuli, except for the 2-part vs. 1-part contrast. The results for the visual paradigm suggested differences in processing across all features apart from large and medium-size stimuli. These results replicate earlier MMN findings that the brain distinguishes pre-attentively changes in sound frequency, amplitude and gap. Together these findings could be interpreted to support the existence of abstract, pre- attentive processing of numerical magnitudes. Highlights • Auditory and visual processing of numerical and non-numerical magnitudes was examined with EEG • Auditory non-numerical magnitudes and medium vs. small dots replicated earlier MMN studies • aMMN and vMMN showed pre-attentive processing of changes in small numerosities 2 vs. 3 and 2 vs. 1 • 2 vs. 1 tone processing was less robust than 2 vs. 3 or the processing of the visual contrasts • The brain processes changes in small non-symbolic magnitudes pre-attentively ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n7f89af0a02c2: Reliable demographic data are critical for seal population assessment and management, yet remain challenging to obtain from drone surveys without automated tools. The pipeline combines cascaded DeepLabV3+ segmentation (water removal, colony-level seal detection, and individual body-contour refinement), principal component analysis (PCA)-based extraction of body length and maximum width, and three-class size-class determination based on body length (pups, juveniles, subadults/adults). The pipeline enables automated demographic monitoring of pinniped haulouts with quantitatively characterized uncertainty across survey conditions. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
n83a80ea0e6ad: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3) is most common subtype of autosomal dominant spinocerebellar ataxia worldwide and the most prevalent CAG expansion disorder in the east Asian population, but disease-modifying therapies remain unavailable. Oral dosing achieved nanomolar cerebellar exposure and showed no overt liver, kidney, or glial toxicity over 28 days. Together, these findings provide preclinical proof of concept that utilizing orally available small molecule compounds to allele-selectively enhance mAtxn3 autophagic degradation for SCA3 treatment. n0e2809c957ac: Thermophilic bacterial lipases must combine structural stability with the conformational flexibility required for interfacial activation, yet the local organization of their metal-binding sites remains incompletely understood. Here, we determined two X-ray crystal structures of the family I.5 lipase from Geobacillus kaustophilus (GkLip). The 2.47-Å orthorhombic model contains a Ca2+ ion at the conserved metal-binding site, whereas the 2.30-Å anisotropic triclinic model contains four non-equivalent protein chains in which no Ca2+ ion was modeled. GkLip retains the canonical α/β-hydrolase fold, the Ser114-Asp318-His359 catalytic triad, the Phe17/Gln115 oxyanion-hole region, an extended lid, and a conserved Zn2+-binding site. In the orthorhombic structure, Gly287, Glu361, Asp366, and Pro367 contribute to the Ca2+ coordination environment. Pro367 adopts a Cγ-endo pucker in the Ca2+-containing structure; three Ca2+-free chains also adopt the endo pucker, whereas one adopts a Cγ-exo pucker. The presence of both Pro367 pucker states in the Ca2+-free structure is consistent with calcium preferentially stabilizing a pre-existing, coordination-compatible conformation. This local organization is further supported by an Arg35-centered network of direct and water-mediated contacts. Comparison with the 94%-identical open G. thermocatenulatus lipase reveals substantial lid rearrangement despite strong conservation of the protein core. Together, these structures highlight localized conformational variability at the calcium-binding region within an otherwise highly conserved thermophilic lipase scaffold. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n6c871dffd7b2: Four rhizobial strains isolated from root nodules of tropical leguminous plants in Costa Rica were characterized. Strain LEGMi-135b was isolated from Lonchocarpus felipei root nodules, LEGMi-12c from Cojoba arborea, LEGMi-198b from Calliandra haematocephala and Rhizobium altiplani LEGMi-166a from Mimosa pigra. Phylogenetic analyses based on the 16S rRNA gene and four concatenated housekeeping genes (recA, atpD, GATase and gyrB) placed these strains within the genera Martinezella (LEGMi-12c, LEGMi-135b, and LEGMi-198b) and Rhizobium (LEGMi-166a). Genome-based analyses showed that strain LEGMi-135b exhibited an average nucleotide identity (ANI) value of 94% and a digital DNA-DNA hybridization (dDDH) value of 53.2% compared with its closest related species, Martinezella hainanensis CCBAU 57015T, supporting its classification as a distinct species. LEGMI-12c exhibited ANI and dDDH values of 98% and 87%, respectively, compared with Martinezella hainanensis CCBAU 57015T. LEGMi-198b showed the highest similarity to Rhizobium cerradonense CNPSo 3464, with ANI and dDDH values of 98% and 81.4%, respectively; however, this taxon has not been validly published. LEGMi-166a exhibited ANI and dDDH values of 100% and 99.3%, respectively, compared with Rhizobium altiplani BR 10423ᵀ, confirming its assignment to this species. Additionally, differentiation of strains LEGMi-135b and LEGMi-198b from their closest phylogenetic relatives was supported by phenotypic, physiological, and biochemical analyses. Based on the combined genomic, phenotypic, and biochemical evidence, we propose the establishment of the novel rhizobial species Martinezella legmii sp. nov., with strain LEGMi-135b designated as the type strain (LEGMi-135bᵀ), and Martinezella ivanii sp. nov., with strain LEGMi-198b designated as the type strain (LEGMi-198bᵀ). This study expands our understanding of rhizobial diversity associated with nitrogen-fixing symbioses, particularly among tropical leguminous plants from Costa Rica ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. nfe3d7e104765: Next-generation sequencing data is compositional in nature and ignoring this fact can significantly impact downstream data analyses. This is especially true in co-occurrence (correlation) networks because compositional data is prone to many false negative correlations. The centered log-ration (clr) transformation is a commonly used compositional data analysis (CoDA) approach that converts compositionally constrained data into real number space. The clr transformed values can subsequently be used in machine learning and statistical analyses such as Spearman or Pearson correlations used to generate co-occurrence networks. Here we show that the necessary zero substitution performed prior to clr transformation can create numerous multicollinearity artefacts. We also show that a newer CoDA approach called the robust centered log-ratio (rclr) eliminates these artefacts in correlation-based network analysis.
nccc15bf34fb0: Functional neural networks emerge as developing neurons form synaptic connections. Revealing how these connections are organized and perturbed in disease requires linking single-neuron connectivity to molecular state across thousands of networks, which is challenging with current methods. We developed COSCO (Connectomics by Sequencing in Cerebral Organoids), combining barcoded monosynaptic rabies tracing with single-cell RNA sequencing to reconstruct over 10,000 networks across organoids. We demonstrate that organoid circuitry self-organizes into stereotyped network motifs governed by cell-intrinsic wiring rules aligning with features of mouse cortical connectivity. Projecting network topology onto transcriptomic space reveals that wiring correlates with cell-adhesion and synaptic gene expression programs. In a Tuberous Sclerosis Complex model, pathological hyperexcitability coincides with topological rewiring: mutant networks become more heterogeneous, driven by the transcriptional distribution of upper layer excitatory cell states. This work establishes cerebral organoids as a model to study self-organization of human connectivity, and its disruption in neurodevelopmental disease. n653d928c161b: Carbapenem-resistant Escherichia coli (CREC) is an emerging global health threat associated with limited treatment options and increased mortality. Here, analysis of 20,331 E. coli genomes from urinary tract infection (UTI) and urine samples identifies phylogroup A sequence type 361 (ST361) as an emerging CREC clone associated with UTI. Phylogenetic and phylodynamic analyses reveal two dominant ST361 clades that emerged in Asia around 2006 and subsequently disseminated intercontinentally. ST361 exhibits near pan-drug resistance, with bla NDM-5 conferring carbapenem resistance. In silico capsule and O-antigen typing reveals a highly conserved Klebsiella -like surface polysaccharide serotype in 95.9% of ST361 genomes, which we show contributes to virulence in UTI and catheter-associated UTI mouse models. Analysis of the mobile genetic elements harbouring bla NDM-5 in ST361 and other CREC further reveals a dynamic interplay between plasmid transfer and insertion elements that contributes to bla NDM-5 dissemination. Together, these findings identify ST361 as an emerging UTI-associated CREC clone and reveal the convergence of clonal expansion, virulence-associated surface architecture and mobile genetic elements in its spread. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n8308c2c39931: Cryo-EM maps frequently suffer from weak structural signals, spatially variable quality, and noise, complicating interpretation and downstream modeling. Existing post-processing approaches treat density enhancement, quality assessment, and masking as separate tasks, often amplifying residual noise or introducing local artifacts. Here, we present CryoCodex, a unified framework that jointly performs density enhancement, local quality estimation, and molecular masking. CryoCodex introduces a multi-head, multi-scale vector-quantization module that projects encoder-derived latent features onto a shared codebook of structural prototypes. By imposing discrete constraints across feature subspaces and spatial scales, the codebook suppresses stochastic noise while preserving recurrent structural patterns. On a non-redundant test set of 126 experimental maps spanning 3–8 Å, CryoCodex outperformed four representative methods, achieving a mean map–model FSC-0.5 of 3.93 Å versus 4.62 Å for EMReady2 and 6.87 Å for the deposited maps. Downstream automated de novo model building with Phenix further confirmed the quality of the CryoCodex-enhanced maps. These gains extended to maps containing nucleic acids, where CryoCodex produced the best map–model agreement and improved model building. Half-map cross-validation indicated that these improvements are anchored to experimental data rather than driven by half-map-specific noise or structural hallucination. CryoCodex also delivered reliable local quality estimates and molecular masks within the same framework. Together, these results establish CryoCodex as a practical tool for cryo-EM map post-processing and structural determination in challenging cases. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. nd48c36122937: While cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has transformed structural biology, sample preparation remains a major determinant of success. Specifically, the air-water interface (AWI) can damage complexes, impose preferred orientation, and reduce particle density. Here, we introduce cryoSHIELDs, a chemically diverse library of peptide additives designed to passivate the AWI and improve cryo-EM grid preparation. Across 24 protein systems spanning GPCRs, ABC and SLC transporters, soluble and Fab-containing complexes, and enzymes, cryoSHIELDs increased the success rate of structure determination. Individual cryoSHIELDs improved particle density, angular sampling, complex stability, and, for routine targets, map quality and resolution. This toolkit enabled the structural characterization of important targets, including the ABCC6 transporter, revealing unique TMD0-mediated stabilization, and DAMGO-bound μ-opioid receptor-Gi complex using substantially lower protein concentration. CryoSHIELDs provide a simple, tunable, and broadly applicable platform for more reliable cryo-EM in discovery biology and structure-based drug development.
n05651a701bc5: Vertebrate cGAS senses DNA and synthesizes cyclic GMP-AMP to launch an immune response through the adaptor protein STING. Bacterial cyclic oligonucleotide-based signaling systems (CBASS) are evolutionarily related to the metazoan cGAS-STING pathway, but the molecular cues triggering bacterial cGAS activation remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a cGAS-like enzyme, termed DancE (DNA-activated di-nucleotide cyclase in Escherichia), that is activated by binding to double-stranded DNA. DancE is repressed by the bacterial chaperone DnaK, which prevents DNA binding by DancE. We further identified lambda phage prohead protease gpC that activates DancE through its protease activity. These results provide an example of a bacterial cGAS-like enzyme that is activated by DNA but through a guard-like mechanism that normally suppresses DNA sensing, suggesting that DNA sensing by cGAS family proteins is an ancient antiviral strategy conserved across kingdoms of life.
n00f7a9fd1ed7: Objective Heme-dependent metronidazole (MTZ) resistance has emerged in Clostridioides difficile and is primarily mediated by a T-to-G single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) in the promoter of nimB (P nimB G). We aimed to develop a CRISPR-Cas12a-based assay for rapid detection of the P nimB G mutation associated with MTZ resistance. Methods A series of primers and CRISPR RNAs (crRNAs) were designed and optimized to identify the most effective combination for discriminating between P nimB G (MTZ-resistant) and P nimB T (MTZ-susceptible) alleles. Detection was evaluated by visual fluorescence using blue-light and UV imaging systems, as well as by quantitative fluorescence measurements. Results The CRISPR-Cas12a assay accurately differentiated P nimB G and P nimB T alleles in C. difficile . In a collection of clinical isolates, the assay correctly identified all 11 MTZ-susceptible isolates carrying the P nimB T allele and all 10 MTZ-resistant isolates carrying the P nimB G allele. Fluorescence signals were readily detected both visually and quantitatively. Furthermore, colony PCR using crude colony lysates yielded results comparable to those obtained with purified genomic DNA, enabling rapid colony-based detection without conventional DNA extraction. Conclusions The CRISPR-Cas12a assay enables rapid molecular detection of the P nimB G mutation associated with heme-dependent MTZ resistance in C. difficile . This approach could complement conventional susceptibility testing for MTZ resistance detection. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
n4e6d4c8936a7: Polyamines are cationic metabolites that support critical cellular processes including transcription, translation, and cell proliferation. Although polyamine synthesis and transport are emerging therapeutic targets in human disease, the polyamine transport system remains poorly understood. ATP13A2-4 were recently identified as endolysosomal polyamine exporters, transporting putrescine (PUT), spermidine (SPD), and spermine (SPM) from the vesicular lumen to the cytosol. Despite interest in pharmacologically targeting these transporters, existing assays of transporter function rely on indirect or endpoint measures that cannot resolve transport as it occurs. Here, we report the first voltage-clamp recordings of polyamine transporter activity, directly detecting ATP13A2- and ATP13A3-mediated charge movement across cell membranes. When expressed in Xenopus oocytes, these transporters localized to the plasma membrane, enabling electrophysiological measurements. Polyamines induced inward currents dependent on transporter catalytic activity, and their dose-dependence correlated with ATPase assays. ATP13A2 currents were largest in response to SPM, whereas ATP13A3 currents were largest with PUT, consistent with their established substrate preferences. Polyamine-induced currents were blocked by the polyamine transport inhibitor AMXT-1501. These findings establish ATP13A2 and ATP13A3 as electrogenic polyamine pumps and demonstrate the utility of two-electrode voltage clamp as a label-free, transporter-resolved assay to complement other approaches in polyamine transporter-targeted drug discovery. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n4e2966ccde05: Voluntary cognitive regulation can increase or decrease pain, but direction-sensitive neural correlates may emerge at different analytical levels. We reanalyzed 3,201 thermal-stimulation trials from 33 participants, integrating 0-200 warmth/pain ratings, regional fMRI activity, and trial-wise lagged coupling. Both instructions shifted ratings in the intended direction, with no reliable difference in mean success. Down-regulation was associated with lower bilateral S2/opercular and insular activity and higher left dlPFC/IFJ activity after FDR correction across 32 regions; run-matched comparisons were weaker and none survived the corresponding correction. Contrast-map Neurologic Pain Signature attenuation did not replicate in a rating-adjusted FWL-LSS trial-wise analysis despite strong temperature sensitivity. Up-regulation success covaried with an exploratory, post selection lagged dlPFC/IFJ-valuation composite (r = -0.546, 95% CI [-0.764, -0.270]). The association exceeded matched reverse-direction, zero-lag, and time-reversed controls, lay outside permutation and circular-shift nulls, and persisted after AR(1) prewhitening. A transition-level analysis across 297 up-regulation transitions preserved a negative success-by-source interaction (adjusted three-target mean beta = -0.163, cluster-bootstrap 95% CI [-0.290, -0.054], Freedman-Lane p = 0.010). Six session-wise DCM variants showed no consistent regulation-versus-passive effective-connectivity effect and did not independently validate an up-specific directed mechanism. These analyses identify a down-regulation-associated regional pattern and a candidate prefrontal-valuation coupling association requiring independent confirmation. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
na21bec7555ff: Although human perception appears continuous, converging evidence suggests that sensory input is integrated over discrete temporal windows. The duration of these Temporal Integration Windows (TIWs) determines the temporal resolution of perception, but how this fundamental property develops across infancy and childhood remains unknown. Here, we estimate TIW duration from 5 months of age to adulthood using a novel, instruction-free eye-tracking paradigm that isolates pre-attentive visual integration. Across four experiments with the same paradigm (N = 308 participants), we measured spontaneous detection of a visual target that emerges only when two alternating displays are integrated within a single perceptual window. We observed a striking developmental shortening of the TIW. In adults and 5-year-olds, integration succeeded at short interstimulus intervals (ISIs; 16-32 ms) but failed at longer intervals (83-116 ms), yielding an estimated TIW of ~57 ms. At 3 years, the TIW extended to ~100 ms. In infancy, integration remained robust at substantially longer ISIs, with estimates of ~250 ms at 18 and 8 months, and ~400 ms at 5 months. The steepest reduction occurred within the first year of life. These findings reveal an approximately sevenfold acceleration in the temporal resolution of visual perception from early infancy to adulthood. Progressive shortening of TIWs suggests that infants and adults integrate sensory information over fundamentally different temporal scales, with implications for perceptual organization, learning, and neurodevelopmental trajectories. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n949895c4ca1a: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly capable of carrying out autonomous computational research, but it remains unclear whether they can develop molecular modeling methods that compete with strong human-developed approaches. Here, we evaluate autonomous method development across four settings: Therapeutics Data Commons (TDC) ADMET tasks, the OpenADMET ExpansionRx Challenge, the activity prediction track of the OpenADMET PXR Induction Challenge, and the Practical Molecular Optimization (PMO) benchmark. Agents followed the prescribed data splits, metrics, and evaluation protocols for each benchmark. On TDC, the best agent-developed score across configurations improved on the leaderboard reference on 18 of 21 tasks and on the combined leaderboard and peer-reviewed reference on 17, while individual Codex configurations improved on the combined reference on 13 tasks. On ExpansionRx, five-agent and single-agent Codex configurations achieved overall scores corresponding to fourth and sixth place relative to the published final leaderboard, with the five-agent configuration reaching top-five performance on seven of nine endpoints. On PXR, five-agent Codex achieved a mean absolute error slightly outperforming the best published challenge entry. On PMO, five-agent Codex developed a molecular optimizer that outperformed existing methods evaluated under the benchmark's standard setup; other methods obtained higher reported scores under modified conditions, including additional molecular pretraining data or a different oracle-call budget. Together, these results show that current LLM agents can autonomously develop high-performing molecular prediction and optimization methods across substantially different drug-discovery settings, in several cases matching or exceeding leading human-developed approaches. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors are employees of and hold equity in Deep Origin Inc., which funded the research described in this work. n7fd6f2c2aa6c: Although largely preventable, cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death worldwide. Synthetic data generation (SDG) of health data can facilitate data sharing for research and development of personalised cardiovascular disease prevention tools. Current state-of-the-art SDG methods are limited to cross-sectional data or focused on short-term or in-patient EHR applications lacking benchmarks for generalisability. Since prevention is a long-term longitudinal objective, these limitations must be addressed. We evaluated two tabular generative adversarial networks, TGAN and CTGAN, for privacy and fidelity on a structured 6-year longitudinal trial dataset within CVD prevention. We compared performance with a rudimentary perturbation method. In addition, we performed a variable-wise evaluation and an age-stratified analysis of the higher performing model to assess preservation of clinically relevant characteristics. Overall, CTGAN showed better fidelity than TGAN. The models performed similarly within privacy, showing better results than the perturbation method. CTGAN had lower performance in comparison to the perturbation method within numerical fidelity of continuous variables and overall temporal fidelity. Furthermore, CTGAN's performance was lower for younger age groups than older. CTGAN shows better than or equal performance within fidelity and privacy than TGAN and the perturbation method on a long-term longitudinal dataset within CVD prevention. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study evaluating CTGAN on a longitudinal dataset and our findings suggest that handling of temporal characteristics and imbalanced subgroups need further refinement. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. nce0a31e891c9: Domestic dogs may influence human microbiota and act as reservoirs or sentinels for zoonotic bacteria, yet little is known about these dynamics in Southeast Asia. Using full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing from rectal swabs, we analyzed microbiota from dog-owner pairs from four villages of rural Thailand (Nan province) to assess microbial diversity, shared taxa, and zoonotic potential. Dogs exhibited higher microbial and putative pathogen diversity than humans, particularly during the rainy season. While dog-owner pairs shared more bacteria than unrelated individuals, overall overlap remained limited - likely driven by their dogs free-roaming lifestyles and broader environmental exposures. However, co-occurrence of putative zoonotic pathogens such as Shigella spp. and Klebsiella pneumoniae suggests dogs could serve as useful indicators for specific public health risks, with further targeted pathogen screening needed to validate these results. Our findings highlight the value of integrating dogs into zoonotic surveillance programs, particularly in regions with free-ranging dog populations and close human-animal contact.
nff52e56a0fff: Focal adhesions (FAs) and actin stress fibers (SFs) are mechanically coupled but often analyzed separately. We present FilAdh, a unified framework for FA instance segmentation, SF instance reconstruction, morphometry, and FA-anchorage-based SF classification. Across 57 held-out HeLa, SUIT-2, and MRC-5 cell line images, FilAdh achieved the highest FA Dice, intersection over union (IoU), and recall and the highest SF clDice and skeleton precision among benchmarked methods; paired t tests with Holm correction indicated significant gains over all compared methods for FA Dice, IoU, and recall, and over classical methods for SF centerline metrics, with no significant differences detected relative to the deep-learning comparators. Conditional on expert-curated FA and SF masks, SFs were assigned to dorsal, ventral, and peripheral classes with 81.5%-87.3% accuracy. Controlled Poisson-Gaussian noise, Gaussian defocus, and point-spread-function blur revealed distinct, structure-specific errors in overlap and object-level measurements. By linking segmentation and reconstruction to count, area, length, apparent width, and structural class, FilAdh offers an interpretable view of the FA-actin structural system and makes degradation-dependent measurement biases explicit. BIGGER PICTURECells sense and respond to their physical environment through focal adhesions and actin stress fibers. The two form a mechanically coupled system, yet they are usually analyzed separately, with workflows re-tuned for each new set of images. FilAdh analyzes both within a single framework, tailoring segmentation, reconstruction, and classification to each structures geometry: compact adhesion patches versus thin, extended fiber networks. Testing on expert-annotated references and under controlled degradations that mimic low signal, focus errors, and optical blur shows that these common imaging imperfections distort adhesion and fiber measurements in different ways. The same design principle--matching the analysis to each structures shape and judging methods by how errors propagate into the final biological measurements--may benefit other bioimage-analysis problems. Released code, trained weights, and fixed data splits make all comparisons reproducible and extensible. n425e080244e0: The balance between excitatory and inhibitory (E/I) neurons is fundamental to cortical function, and its disruption underlies a wide range of neurological disorders, including epilepsy, Alzheimer’s disease and autism spectrum disorder. Cortical organoids offer a promising model to study this balance, as they recapitulate key features of brain development, including the emergence of E/I circuitry. However, no existing technology can simultaneously resolve neuronal identity, spatial organization, and dynamic network activity within intact organoids, limiting precise interrogation of E/I circuit function. Here, we report INFORM, an INtegrated Flexible Organoid Recording Multimodal neural interface that conformally wraps organoids of any size and shape, enabling long-term recordings over 371 days with above 90% of channels detecting spikes. INFORM interface combines four distinct modalities; electrophysiology, two-photon calcium imaging, targeted electrical microstimulation, and chemical intervention to monitor and modulate neural activity across multiple spatial and temporal scales spanning from action potentials from single neurons to synchronized bursts from large-scale populations. Such high-resolution interrogation enables probing of emergence of functional connectivity in fusing assembloids and resolves spatially discrete functional subnetworks that can be selectively recruited and modulated by INFORM. Neurotransmission blockade confirms that stimulus-evoked suppression of neuronal spiking is mediated by GABAergic inputs providing direct functional evidence of the presence of inhibitory signaling in organoids. This work allows single-cell dissection of functional networks in brain organoids, providing a powerful platform for modelling and studying cortical development, neurological diseases, and the E/I imbalances underlying circuit dysfunction. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
n13c34d7c13bb: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) is a powerful approach for measuring the transcriptomic landscape at single-cell resolution. However, while scRNA-seq data reveals what genes each cell expresses, they do not indicate where that cell was located within the tissue or organ, anatomically. We developed FlyAnatoView ( https://www.flyrnai.org/tools/rna_seq_base/web/svg_files/ ), a resource that projects scRNA-seq data onto anatomical diagrams, restoring this missing spatial context.
nf9b6de3df28b: Neurodegenerative proteinopathies are defined by distinct proteins whose folding, trafficking and clearance depend on shared proteostasis machinery. Whether these disorders engage common components or only common processes has been unresolved. We mapped 16 disease proteins from 12 disorders onto a fixed 990-protein proteostasis network. Across the 12 disorders, the neighborhoods of these proteins shared specific proteins beyond expectations from process composition and connectivity. The same held for the two disorders defined by more than one protein. Nine proteins contributed disproportionately, and only autophagy’s removal significantly reduced similarity. Removing PRKN, HSPA8 or UBQLN2 in silico reduced path efficiency, marking them candidate shared network vulnerabilities. In human brain proteomes, Alzheimer’s disease-zone proteins showed greater abundance remodeling in the insoluble fraction; recurrence across disorders showed no such association. The result is a component-level architecture prioritizing network-derived candidates for cross-disease functional testing.
n6d2842502386: Fosfomycin is increasingly used to treat multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections, yet resistance surveillance largely relies on homology-based detection of known fos genes. Here, we identify Gfa, a previously unrecognized integron-borne fosfomycin resistance determinant uncovered through functional screening of 129 integron gene cassettes. Gfa confers high-level fosfomycin resistance across Enterobacterales and Pseudomonas aeruginosa and is resistant to phosphonoformate inhibition. Structural modelling and mutagenesis reveal a conserved cysteine-rich, zinc-organized architecture essential for activity and distinct from canonical Fos enzymes. Crude-extract assays confirm glutathione-dependent fosfomycin inactivation under metal-chelating conditions. Distant Gfa homologs also conferred resistance, although activity was restricted to a subset of proteins tested. Together, these findings establish Gfa as a previously unrecognized fosfomycin resistance family and highlight the limitations of homology-based mining for discovering novel resistance determinants and predicting which family members are functional. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. nade51682b6cc: Enterobacterales pathogens that encode multiple carbapenemase genes are an emerging public health threat. The genomic and plasmid context of the multi-carbapenemase producers has not yet been explored at scale. We analysed 1501 publicly-available global genomes that encoded two or more genes from the five prevalent carbapenemase families (IMP, KPC, NDM, OXA-48-like, and VIM). We observed 241 distinct allelic combinations, with NDM/OXA-48-like (25.6%), multiple KPC (25.3%), KPC/NDM (18.8%), and multiple NDM (10.9%) being the most common groups. We found that many genomes were part of high-risk lineages (48.0%). Most genomes carried carbapenemase genes on two plasmids (59.2%) or one plasmid (23.5%), and most genomes encoded different carbapenemase families (56.2%) rather than copies of the same allele (36.2%). We observed multiple mechanisms of multi-carbapenemase evolution including plasmid co-integration, convergence with virulence, and generation of novel allele diversity through duplication. Multi-carbapenemase plasmids had more AMR genes that conferred resistance to more AMR classes compared to plasmids encoding a single carbapenemase. The proportion of cross-class combinations (KPC/NDM and NDM/OXA-48-like) increased significantly over time, with NDM-5/OXA-181 (3.3-fold) and NDM-4/OXA-181 (8.9-fold) combinations enriched. These findings provide valuable insights into the genomic features of multi-carbapenemase Enterobacterales to support the development of effective surveillance programmes.
n9952f4bb69d1: Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a leading cause of community acquired pneumonia and bronchitis in people, particularly children and young adults. Like many bacterial pathogens, M. pneumoniae can grow in biofilm towers on both biotic and abiotic surfaces. Current models indicate that planktonic M. pneumoniae are simply individual cells that are dispersed from biofilm towers due to physical shear forces, and do not represent a bona fide planktonic growth state. However recent data indicate that these fractions may be physiologically distinct and may differentially influence disease outcome. We observed that experimental infection of mice with inoculum containing both adherent and non-adherent fractions of M. pneumoniae produced more severe lung pathology than inoculum prepared from M. pneumoniae adherent biofilms alone. Direct comparison of experimental infection with titer matched non-adherent (P-Mp) and adherent (B-Mp) fractions revealed that P-Mp produces more severe lung pathology compared to infection with B-Mp. Furthermore, experimental infection with a lower dose of P-Mp resulted in similar lung pathology relative to B-Mp infected mice. This increase in pathology was not associated with differences in bacterial burden, bacterial dispersal during inoculum preparation, nor due to differences in the phenotype of host immune responses. Comparative proteomics revealed that certain known and putative virulence factors associated with immune evasion are upregulated in P-Mp, potentially explaining the difference in virulence between the two fractions. Furthermore, comparative proteomics revealed distinct metabolic phenotypes between the two fractions, consistent with distinct planktonic and biofilm growth states, indicating that P-Mp likely represents a bona fide planktonic growth state. Collectively, these data implicate the growth state of M. pneumoniae as a determinant of in vivo virulence for this atypical human pathogen. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
n06912f40078d: Many termites digest lignocellulosic wood using diverse gut microbiota, yet functions are rarely linked to specific symbionts because complete genomes are scarce. We used PacBio HiFi long reads to reconstruct circular single-contig bacterial metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) from the gut microbiota of the wood-feeding termite Nasutitermes takasagoensis . From 13.9 Gb of HiFi data, we obtained highly contiguous assemblies, including 11 Breznakiellaceae (Spirochaetota), two Candidatus Fibrimonas (Fibrobacterota), and one Chitinispirillaceae genome, three dominant lineages in this gut ecosystem. The reconstructed genomes encoded extensive carbohydrate-active enzyme repertoires and anaerobic fermentation pathways consistent with lignocellulose degradation. They also carried genes for essential amino acid biosynthesis, while nitrogen-fixation capacity was present in representatives of all three lineages but varied among closely related strains. One Breznakiellaceae genome possessed a complete Wood-Ljungdahl pathway potentially supporting reductive acetogenesis in the presence of external formate, whereas related strains carried incomplete variants likely involved in anabolic C1 metabolism. Differences in CAZymes, C1 metabolism, and nitrogen fixation among closely related strains reveal functional diversification that fragmented MAGs would not resolve. The mapping of metatranscriptomic reads from three biological replicates of the fiber-associated community to the reconstructed genomes provided independent evidence that key predicted metabolic functions are transcriptionally active. Our results demonstrate the power of HiFi metagenomics to recover highly contiguous genomes from complex insect microbiomes and uncover lineage-specific metabolic roles of dominant termite gut symbionts. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. nc7d39cb027b7: Spontaneous spinal cord regeneration is an endogenous process operational in diverse vertebrate and select mammalian species. Yet despite resulting in functional regeneration, axonal regrowth dynamics as well as underlying molecular programs are largely unknown. Live-cell imaging following laser axotomy of individual zebrafish spinal cord M-cell axons reveals a time-sensitive multistep process. From a genetic screen we uncover previously unrecognized roles for two evolutionary conserved genes, celsr3 and huntingtin (htt) in spontaneous spinal cord regeneration. Specifically, we find that htt is critical to initiate a transcriptional injury response in regenerating M-cells, enabling their axon to traverse the injury site. Once axons cross the injury site celsr3 functions to increase growth rates, while both celsr3 and htt function to sustain long-range axonal growth. Moreover, we show that htt is dispensable for optic nerve and peripheral motor neuron regeneration, and that reducing soma-to-injury site distance in htt mutant M-cell axons partially restores regeneration, demonstrating a selective role in long-range CNS axon regeneration. Consistent with a transport-based mechanism, genetic knockdown of htt-associated axonal transport proteins recapitulates the htt mutant regeneration phenotype. Combined, our results provide compelling evidence for a time and distance-sensitive multistep molecular framework in which celsr3 dependent growth rate modulation and htt dependent axonal transport promote spontaneous, long-range spinal cord regeneration.
n3075baac2abd: Parkinson's disease (PD) gait is characterized by reduced walking speed, short shuffling steps, increased double stance time, and increased step time variability. The most debilitating symptom in PD is freezing of gait (FOG), a context-dependent locomotion arrest, mostly occurring while encountering turns, obstacles, and narrow pathways. FOG is more pronounced during turning, a complex task that challenges motor planning and execution. Here, we simulate this phenomenon using a computational model inspired by the cortico-basal ganglia circuitry, based on reinforcement learning (RL) principles. In the model, the agent was trained to learn a value profile while navigating a path that involved turning. To simulate PD conditions, we clamped the temporal difference (TD) error, typically associated with dopaminergic signaling. Our model results show that compared to healthy controls (HC), PD non-freezers and PD freezers exhibit a reduction in turning velocity and step length, alongside an attenuated compensatory step-width widening at the sharpest turn, more pronounced in PD freezers, who additionally show increased step time variability. These kinematic impairments worsen during tighter turns. Ultimately, this model implicates FOG as a problem of impaired estimation of value over space and could potentially represent a generalized deficit in gait impairments in PD. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
n01a8245d43e3: Zoonotic influenza A viruses pose constitute a significant persistent threat to global public health, yet quantitative approaches for assessing their cross-species transmission potential remain limited. Here, we present InfluProto, a deep learning model that introduces prototype learning into host prediction for influenza A virus, framing conceptualizing host adaptation as a continuous process rather than a discrete outcome. InfluProto embeds viral sequences into a continuous representation space anchored by human, swine, and avian prototypes, using cosine distances as a quantitative measure of host adaptation. InfluProto accurately discriminated among the three host classes, achieving recall and precision exceeding 0.97, and substantially outperformed conventional classification models models--particularly on challenging zoonotic strains, including the 2009 pandemic H1N1 (pdm09) lineage. Beyond host classification, the learned representations captured biologically meaningful host-adaptive signatures,; notably, with pdm09 viruses occupying occupied an intermediate position between human and swine clusters, consistent with their evolutionary origin. Analysis of simulated reassortment further revealed that the introduction of human-origin segments into swine influenza viruses reduced their distance to the human prototype, indicating that InfluProto can detect reassortment-associated shifts in host adaptation. To facilitate broad public useaccess, we have developed an interactive web service for InfluProto. Collectively, our work establishes a continuous framework for characterizing host adaptation and evaluating zoonotic risk in influenza A viruses, with potential implications for pandemic surveillance and preparedness.
ne13285ff37a0: Communities living in biodiversity hotspots are at increased risk of pathogen exposure and spread due to insufficient access to nutrition, clean water, and sanitation. Viruses, in particular, have high epidemic and spillover potential, and widespread health impacts, yet, viral diversity and dynamics remain understudied in many high-risk regions. In Madagascar, a hotspot with unparalleled biodiversity, socioeconomic constraints, and a heavy burden of infectious diseases, ongoing healthcare initiatives provide opportunities to survey circulating viral diversity. Here, we used a metagenomic workflow to characterize the viromes of oral/nasal swabs from febrile individuals visiting a mobile healthcare clinic in southeastern Madagascar, of which 49% were malaria-positive (Plasmodium falciparum). We characterized sequences of human-infecting viruses from twelve families (Adenoviridae, Anelloviridae, Orthoherpesviridae, Papillomaviridae, Polyomaviridae, Astroviridae, Coronaviridae, Matonaviridae, Orthomyxoviridae, Paramyxoviridae, Picornaviridae, and Sedoreoviridae). These viral sequences generally showed high similarity to known lineages circulating globally, but multiple viruses considered rare or emerging were identified (e.g. enterovirus C105, enterovirus C117). While we did not detect a significant association between malaria status and pathogenic virus presence, younger individuals had higher odds of having a pathogenic virus. Nonpathogenic viruses in Anelloviridae were prevalent and diverse with richness ranging from 0 to 70. Individuals with P. falciparum or a pathogenic virus tended to share more anelloviruses. We also detected viruses that are protist-associated, plant-infecting, or with unknown hosts. Overall, our work documents extensive viral diversity in Madagascar, highlighting how metagenomic workflows can be used to build viral genomic resources for pathogen surveillance in regions with high infectious disease burden.
n54eb4090e2d3: Metagenomic sequencing enables broad pathogen detection without requiring prior assumptions about the organisms present, but the memory and computational demands of classifying large sequencing datasets against reference databases often lead analysis pipelines to rely on desktop or server-grade computing platforms. We present KENT, a portable edge-computing framework for metagenomic pathogen screening based on a cluster of NVIDIA Jetson Nano modules. KENT adapts CuCLARK-l for low-memory embedded execution and extends it with a custom software stack for distributed read classification, abundance estimation, split-run abundance merging, and report generation. Using an MPI-based controller/responder architecture, KENT supports local, offline analysis with sample-level parallelism across multiple nodes. We evaluate KENT using long read wastewater metagenomic samples with a custom pathogen database and the CAMI2 Marine long read dataset. In the wastewater setting, KENT achieves an average speedup of 3.1 × over the CPU-based CLARK-l baseline while maintaining close agreement in classified read abundance estimates. On CAMI2 Marine, KENT achieves an average speedup of 2.68 × and similarly preserves CLARK-l abundance profiles. Evaluation against the CAMI2 long read taxonomic ground truth yields a mean species-level precision of 58.55%, recall of 93.36%, F1 score of 71.74%, and L1 abundance distance of 0.731, closely matching CLARK-l. Among ground truth species represented in the reference database, KENT detects 99.86% on average. A controlled database-size experiment further shows little change in classification throughput across the tested database configurations, while large sequencing inputs remain constrained by the Jetson Nano’s unified memory capacity. Overall, KENT demonstrates that GPU-accelerated metagenomic classification can be adapted to low-memory embedded hardware while preserving the biological profiling behavior of the CLARK-l baseline, supporting portable and offline pathogen screening in resource-constrained settings. nd754b81957c2: Free recall of naturalistic stimuli, such as films and stories, reveals what people remember and how they organize it. Scoring such recall requires matching each recalled utterance to the encoded stimulus, and doing this manually often makes large studies impractical. Existing automated methods mostly return similarity or aggregate scores rather than explicit matches between recalled and stimulus content. Here we introduce an open-source, model-agnostic pipeline that uses a large language model (LLM) to divide the stimulus and the recall into information units and to match units between the two texts. The output is a table of unit-to-unit matches with accuracy labels, from which standard analysis scripts compute recall measures. We validated the pipeline with four LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT 5.4, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Gemini 2.5 Flash) on three datasets. On typed recall of four short stories, agreement between each model and two trained raters ({phi} = .73-.79) was close to the agreement between the raters themselves ({phi} = .77). A second run reproduced each model's matches ({phi} = .91-.97) more closely than the raters agreed with each other. On spoken recall of 10 films, every model attributed recall to the correct film with high agreement. On uncorrected speech-to-text recall of a television episode, agreement varied more across models. The median cost was under $1 per participant for every model. These results suggest that the pipeline can serve as a reliable, low-cost alternative to manual scoring of free recall.
nb5a5cb7d388b: Frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD), predominantly comprised of tau and TDP-43 proteinopathies, is a common cause of early-onset dementia. Biomarkers that reliably classify FTLD subtypes are limited, thereby hindering in-vivo diagnosis and clinical trial stratification. We conducted large-scale, multi-platform cerebrospinal fluid proteomics in 566 individuals, including 274 FTLD-spectrum (48 autopsy-confirmed FTLD-TDP, 90 autopsy-confirmed FTLD-tau), 171 Alzheimer’s disease, and 95 controls. In neuropathological subtype contrasts, elevated matrix metalloproteinase MMP10 classified Pick’s disease (PiD) versus other subtypes with near-perfect accuracy across proteomic platforms. We further validated CSF MMP10 as a potential PiD diagnostic biomarker via a targeted immunoassay in an independent, autopsy-confirmed FTLD cohort. Post-synaptic proteins HOMER1 and DLG4 exhibited elevations across FTLD-TDP subtypes (A, B, and C) versus FTLD-tau. Network analysis identified RNA metabolism and pro-inflammatory signatures in FTLD-TDP, and cytoskeletal and heat shock signatures in progressive supranuclear palsy. These findings reveal candidate diagnostic biomarkers and proteomic pathways underlying FTLD clinico-pathological heterogeneity.
nad30c85e1599: Background . Influenza remains a major cause of global morbidity and mortality. Pharmacodynamic biomarkers that quantify treatment response within the lung could accelerate influenza therapeutic development. We evaluated [ 18 F]-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography ([ 18 F]-FDG-PET) as a non-invasive biomarker of antiviral efficacy. Methods . Serial [ 18 F]-FDG-PET was evaluated in two murine H1N1 influenza models using mouse-adapted PR8 strain and CA-09 clinical isolate following treatment with favipiravir, baloxavir marboxil, or ribavirin. PET measures were compared with pulmonary viral burden, inflammatory cytokine expression, computed tomography (CT) imaging, and respiratory function measured by whole-body plethysmography (WBP). Results . Antiviral treatment in PR8 infection model reduced lung [ 18 F]-FDG uptake by 27-49% and metabolic lung volume (MLV) by 40.5-74.6% (both p < 0.001). Antiviral response was detectable as early as 3 days post-infection, when uptake decreased by 28.7-53.2% and MLV by 33.8-75.0%. Lung uptake also strongly correlated with MLV (r = 0.93, p < 0.001) and with pulmonary viral burden and inflammatory mediators. These findings were reproduced in a model of pandemic H1N1/CA-09, where baloxavir reduced uptake by 37.4% (p = 0.02) and MLV by 67.5% (p < 0.001) at day 3. In both models, changes in [ 18 F]-FDG-PET parameters preceded improvements in lung CT and respiratory function. Conclusions . Lung [ 18 F]-FDG-PET provides an early, quantitative measure of antiviral response in experimental influenza, supporting its further evaluation as a translational pharmacodynamic endpoint.
n209b0107427e: Inflammatory activation remodels the Golgi apparatus to meet increased secretory demand, yet whether these structural changes carry computationally accessible information about immune cell state has not been explored. Here we show that machine learning applied to imaging flow cytometry images of the Golgi can distinguish lipopolysaccharide (LPS) treated from control cells. We trained models on Golgi images from human THP-1 monocytes before and 16 h after LPS stimulation in vitro, and from circulating myeloid cells of mice 24 h after intratracheal LPS or saline in vivo. In each dataset, the best-performing model was a deep learning model trained directly on images rather than a classifier using predefined morphometric features. Cross-domain performance varied with the model, transfer direction and use of labelled target data: several deep learning models trained on mouse images classified THP-1 cells above chance without changing model parameters. Grad-CAM highlighted regions within or adjacent to the GM130 fluorescence pattern. These findings indicate that GM130 images carry information associated with LPS treatment that supports classification within and across the two datasets. To our knowledge, this is the first application of supervised deep learning to imaging flow cytometry images of a subcellular organelle for inflammatory phenotyping, establishing organelle level image analysis as a potential complement to molecular assays for immune cell classification. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
nd12d70a0c0ad: Metals are essential for all forms of life and are therefore the subject of tight competition at the host-pathogen interface. Manganese (Mn) is an important cofactor for enzymes involved in various processes in bacteria, including the response to oxidative stress, and the ability to scavenge Mn through the expression of high-affinity Mn transporters has been associated with virulence of many extracellular and vacuolar pathogens. While the cytosol has been established to be restrictive for growth of non-adapted pathogens, the extent to which metal limitation contributes to this is not well understood. Here, we investigate whether high-affinity Mn acquisition is important for intracellular adaptation and virulence of the cytosolic pathogen Listeria monocytogenes (Lmo). To do so, we generated a strain of Lmo in which both of its predicted high-affinity Mn transporters, MntH and MntABC, are disrupted. We found that this strain was severely defective in growth in vitro under Mn-limited conditions and had lower intracellular Mn content. Additionally, we observed Mn-dependent transcriptional regulation of the mntH and mntA genes. Together, these data strongly support that MntH and MntABC are high-affinity Mn transporters and are likely to be the only such dedicated Mn transporters expressed in Lmo. Using the {Delta}mntH {Delta}mntA strain, we provide evidence that Mn limitation sensitizes Lmo to oxidative stress in vitro, consistent with the known role of Mn in mitigating reactive oxygen species. Ultimately, we demonstrate that expression of high-affinity Mn transporters is essential for intracellular replication of Lmo in macrophages, plaquing on fibroblast monolayers, and for virulence in an animal model of systemic infection. Our work, therefore, suggests that Lmo is challenged by Mn limitation in the cytosol and requires Mn scavenging to adapt to its intracellular niche.
nb8acc3e8e9a3: Despite lacking a dedicated structural function, brain tissue is exposed to severe mechanical loading during accidents and trauma, with potentially permanent or lethal consequences. Therefore, characterizing its mechanical behavior assumes particular importance for designing protective equipment, planning surgeries, and training neurosurgeons, tasks that often rely on physical brain replicas made from phantom materials. Although the mechanics of brain tissue has been extensively studied, the selection of suitable phantom materials still relies on simplified metrics that fail to capture the highly nonlinear and rate-dependent behavior of the brain. In this work, we characterize the mechanical response at low-to-medium strain rates of common synthetic brain phantom materials, including Sylgard 527, Ecoflex Gel, and a composite hydrogel, and establish rigorous comparisons with porcine brain tissue as a benchmark. To this end, we employ a multi-step stress relaxation protocol under both uniaxial extension and compression across two different strain rates, introduce thermodynamic metrics, and perform comparisons based on rigorous statistical analysis. In particular, we isolate the thermodynamic equilibrium stress-strain curves, representing the baseline material's response, from rate-dependent dissipative inelastic effects, relatable to viscoelastic and poroelastic mechanisms. Our results provide a thorough comparison, revealing critical limitations in existing simulant materials and highlighting significant space for developing improved brain surrogates. The comprehensive dataset collected can also support the calibration of constitutive models, enhancing the predictive accuracy of numerical simulations involving brain tissue and its surrogates. More broadly, this study highlights the need to move beyond simplistic, scalar-metric-based comparisons of mechanical responses across materials.
n67ebeaf2589b: HSV-1 is a neurotropic human pathogen that establishes lifelong latency in sensory neurons. Periodic reactivation causes mucocutaneous lesions and, in some cases, severe corneal and neurological disease. While HSV-1 utilizes numerous viral proteins to extensively reprogram host signaling pathways and evade antiviral responses, how it alters host cytokine receptor networks remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that HSV-1 infection selectively downmodulates multiple members of the gp130 (glycoprotein 130) cytokine receptor family, including gp130, Oncostatin M receptor {beta} (OSMR-{beta}), and leukemia inhibitory factor receptor (LIFR), while sparing IL-6Ra and CNTFRa (Ciliary Neurotrophic Factor Receptor). Because gp130 is the central signaling component of the IL-6 cytokine family and mediates JAK/STAT3 activation, its elimination likely represents a viral strategy to suppress inflammatory and antiviral signaling. Consistent with this, HSV-1 does not induce IL-6 mRNA expression in productively infected cells, suggesting coordinated inhibition of both cytokine production and receptor availability. Mechanistically, we found that the viral RNase VHS is at least partially responsible for gp130 family receptor downmodulation, likely in combination with virus-induced endocytosis/degradation pathways. Functionally, activation of gp130 signaling significantly impairs HSV-1 infection, demonstrating that suppression of antiviral cytokine responses is critical for virus replication. Finally, we determined that CNTF causes reactivation of latent HSV-1 using the LUHMES in vitro latency model, illustrating CNTFRa signaling contribution to latency and reactivation. A similar effect has been reported for IL-6. Together, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized immune evasion mechanism by which HSV-1 remodels gp130 cytokine signaling to promote infection.
n23e795b898e9: Neural activity during performance of a cognitive or motor task is often described as lying on a low-dimensional manifold in the space of all possible activity patterns. When multiple tasks are performed, an individual brain region's activity may generate multiple such manifolds. Several models have been introduced to explain this capability, each with different assumptions concerning architecture and inputs. Here, we develop a theory of multi-tasking according to which models and experimental paradigms can be organized. We introduce a distinction between sequential and simultaneous multi-tasking, the performance of one task at a time or multiple in parallel. We show that interference between tasks often prevents multi-tasking and introduce a model of ``task barcodes" that circumvents this problem and parameterizes a neuronal population's task selectivity. Our theory reveals categorical distinctions between neural circuit mechanisms supporting multi-tasking that can be probed using physiological recordings. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n31368199fbba: Motif scaffolding builds a protein around a prescribed structural motif -- an active site, a binding epitope, a metal site -- so that the motif is presented in its required geometry. The task is usually posed with the motif pinned down: its position along the sequence is given, and several rigid fragments inherit their mutual pose from a native structure. Many applications supply neither. We present NomadFlow, unindexed multi-motif scaffolding on all-atom SE(3) flow matching: the motif enters as a condition, a group projection preserves the internal geometry of each group exactly, and the groups move freely relative to one another until a set time, after which they act only as a condition. We assemble a preliminary benchmark for this setting, varying the granularity of the partition and the structural context around the motif, and obtain unique successes on 19 of 21 tasks. The trained model proposes a diversity of valid mutual poses, and on several tasks the native arrangement is among them. The shape of that solution space, however, varies strongly with the geometry of the condition: across tasks the successful layouts form a wide cloud, collapse onto the native pose, or contract to a connected low-dimensional family -- a continuum of poses rather than a set of isolated solutions. Multi-motif methods are therefore better compared by the space of layouts they propose and the successful part of it they retain than by yield or fold diversity alone. n9a8b9d037c67: Infectious bronchitis virus (IBV) is an economically important avian gammacoronavirus. IBV uses sialic acids and heparan sulfate for cellular attachment, but the host proteins governing its infection remain poorly defined. Here, we investigated the roles of angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) and transmembrane serine protease 2 (TMPRSS2) during IBV Beaudette (IBV BD) infection. ACE2 knockout impaired IBV replication in DF-1 cells, whereas ACE2 reconstitution restored infection. Furthermore, ACE2 overexpression enhanced infection of DF-1 and primary chicken embryo kidney cells, supporting the role of chicken ACE2 as a proviral host factor. In contrast, TMPRSS2 exerted a restrictive function on IBV BD infection as demonstrated in TMPRSS2 KO DF-1 cells and upon pharmacological inhibition, which significantly increased IBV BD infection in DF-1 and Vero cells. RNA sequencing revealed significant changes in lipid metabolism and membrane-related processes following TMPRSS2 knockout and pharmacological inhibition. These findings highlight the opposing roles of ACE2 and TMPRSS2 in IBV BD infection, emphasizing the combined impact of proviral host factors, protease activity, and the cellular membrane environment during gammacoronavirus infections. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. ne183d937eead: Mice are widely used to study the neural basis of perceptual decision-making, often with the ultimate goal of extrapolating insights to humans. Yet, whether humans and mice rely on similar computational strategies remains rarely tested, partly because the two species acquire knowledge differently. Animals learn from experience, while humans usually receive verbal task instructions. Here, we explicitly contrast these modes of learning in humans who perform a perceptual decision-making task adapted from a standardized rodent task. Specifically, we present an open behavioral dataset from 80 human participants who performed 600 trials of a visual contrast-discrimination task, matched to the standardized International Brain Laboratory task for mice (International Brain Laboratory et al., 2021, 2025). Participants either received verbal instructions ('Instructed') or were only told to discover the rules of the task by playing ('Uninstructed'). The dataset contains choices, response times, continuous cursor trajectories, eye-tracking and pupil recordings. Descriptive analyses show that Uninstructed participants were less accurate and had higher lapse rates than Instructed participants. They improved over the first 200 trials, approaching the performance of Instructed participants. These data provide a benchmark for testing whether computational strategies identified in mice also describe human behavior.
n8011832c42d7: Adoptive cellular therapies can be effective against solid tumors but rely on the identification and expansion of rare tumor-reactive T cells (TRTs). Here, we utilize antigen-presenting cell-mimetic scaffolds (APC-ms), a modular biomaterial platform that presents defined peptide-HLA and co-stimulatory ligands on a fluid lipid bilayer to selectively recover rare antigen-specific T cells from peripheral blood. Independent variation of peptide-HLA, co-stimulatory ligands, and cytokine support defined a formulation that enriched MART-1-specific T cells to above 2% of CD8+ T cells in 35 of 50 HLA-A*02:01+ healthy donors from low or undetectable baseline frequencies. Compared with mo-DCs, APC-ms achieved greater fold expansion of MART-1-specific T cells with increased functional avidity and preservation of an early differentiation phenotype, and generated a higher number of MART-1-specific clonotypes. In five of eight patients with treatment-naive melanoma, APC-ms could enrich MART-1-specific T cells to a median of 13.7% of CD8+ cells (range 0.30 - 57.2%) Moreover, APC-ms could expand T cells specific for an HLA-A*24:01-restricted personal neoantigen that were previously undetectable in peripheral blood of a patient with melanoma. These findings establish APC-ms as a tunable platform for the recovery of rare TRTs from peripheral blood, supporting its further development for therapeutic TCR discovery and personalized adoptive cell therapy. ### Competing Interest Statement CJW holds equity in BioNTech, Inc, and is a SAB member of Aethon Therapeutics, Adventris, Repertoire and Natures Toolbox.
